purpose: Add eight source-exact Fanny Crosby hymn excerpts for worship, assurance, holiness, comfort, the cross, and hope.

defaults.author: Fanny Crosby
defaults.sourceTitle: Bells at Evening and Other Verses
defaults.rightsBasis: This 1898 Biglow & Main edition is public domain in the United States; every excerpt is verified against the stored Library of Congress OCR and should be checked against the page scan before publication.

entries.title: More Like Jesus
entries.text: More like Jesus would I be ; Let my Saviour dwell with me, Fill my soul with peace and love, Make me gentle as the dove ;
entries.slideText: More like Jesus would I be ; Let my Saviour dwell with me
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed hymn prayer when preaching about growth in Christlike character.
entries.reviewNote: This is devotional poetry, not Scripture. Explain sanctification and Christlikeness directly from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Jesus Dear, I Come to Thee
entries.text: Jesus dear, I come to Thee, Thou hast said I may ; Tell me what my life should be, Take my sins away ;
entries.slideText: Jesus dear, I come to Thee, Thou hast said I may
entries.sourceLocator: Jesus, Dear, I Come to Thee, page 155
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed invitation hymn excerpt after explaining Christ's welcome and forgiveness from Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: Do not substitute the hymn for a clear Gospel explanation. Present repentance, faith, and forgiveness using KJV Scripture.

entries.title: Safe in the Arms of Jesus
entries.text: Safe in the arms of Jesus, Safe on His gentle breast, There by His love o'ershaded, Sweetly my soul shall rest.
entries.slideText: Safe in the arms of Jesus, Safe on His gentle breast
entries.sourceLocator: Safe in the Arms of Jesus, page 156
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed comfort-hymn excerpt in messages about Christ's care and the believer's rest.
entries.reviewNote: Avoid building assurance on sentiment alone. Establish security and rest from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Near the Cross
entries.text: Near the Cross I'll watch and wait. Hoping, trusting ever.
entries.slideText: Near the Cross I'll watch and wait. Hoping, trusting ever.
entries.sourceLocator: Jesus, Keep Me Near the Cross, page 169
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed hymn stanza in a Christ-centered message about remembering the cross and persevering in hope.
entries.reviewNote: The cross must be explained through Scripture as Christ's finished sacrifice, not merely used as an emotional symbol.

entries.title: Blessed Assurance
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed assurance-hymn excerpt after teaching salvation and the Spirit's witness from Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: Do not imply that singing the words supplies assurance. Ground assurance in Christ, the Gospel, and the cited KJV texts.

entries.title: This Is My Story
entries.text: This is my story, this is my song, Praising my Saviour all the day long.
entries.slideText: This is my story, this is my song, Praising my Saviour all the day long.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed congregational-praise line or testimony transition.
entries.reviewNote: Christian testimony should direct attention to Christ rather than self. Define continual praise through the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: I Shall Know Him
entries.text: I shall know Him, I shall know Him, And alone by His side I shall stand ; I shall know Him, I shall know Him, By the print of the nails in His hand.
entries.slideText: I shall know Him, I shall know Him, By the print of the nails in His hand.
entries.sourceLocator: My Saviour First of All chorus, page 202
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed hymn refrain in messages about seeing Christ and resurrection hope.
entries.reviewNote: Poetic descriptions of heaven must remain subordinate to Scripture. Avoid asserting details beyond the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Till Then I'll Watch and Wait
entries.text: Some day, — till then I'll watch and wait, My lamp all trimmed and burning bright, That when my Saviour opes the gate. My soul to Him may wing its flight.
entries.slideText: Some day, — till then I'll watch and wait, My lamp all trimmed and burning bright
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed closing stanza in a message about watchfulness and hope in Christ's return.
entries.reviewNote: The lamp and gate language is poetic. Explain readiness and the blessed hope from the cited KJV passages without date-setting.
